 K-Beauty Innovation: Kolmar Korea Secures Patent for Dissolvable Hyaluronic Acid Powder That Enhances Skin Absorption 
 by Shin So Young 
 Updated 2026/11/05 11:19 
 A Kolmar Korea researcher is conducting a test of hyaluronic acid powder. Photo provided by Kolmar Korea 
 Kolmar Korea said on the 29th that it had developed Korea's first powdered cosmetic ingredient, hyaluronic acid powder, which dissolves and is absorbed when applied to and rubbed into the skin, and had obtained a patent for the related technology.
Hyaluronic acid is an ingredient widely used to moisturize the skin. Kolmar Korea turned it into crystals shaped like tiny needles to help active ingredients penetrate the skin when they come into contact with it.
The technology applies the principle of existing spicule cosmetics, which use tiny needle-shaped ingredients to stimulate the skin and help active ingredients penetrate. Spicules are natural materials in the form of tiny needles obtained from marine sponges. They are characterized by a prickling sensation immediately after application, but because they are hard materials that do not dissolve in water, they raised concerns about skin irritation and had the inconvenience of requiring users to wash them off after use.
Through more than four years of research, Kolmar Korea developed a process for solidifying hyaluronic acid particles into hard crystals and producing them as pointed powder particles measuring 250㎛. Like existing spicules, the powder comes into contact with the skin's surface to help active ingredients penetrate, but because hyaluronic acid dissolves when it encounters moisture, it does not need to be washed off separately, the company explained.
The method of use is simple. Place the powder on the skin and gently rub it in with your hands. In Kolmar Korea's experiments, the powder showed up to 62% greater moisturizing longevity than a regular cream.
Kolmar Korea plans to launch skincare products incorporating the technology. It is also developing products containing retinol, Centella asiatica extract and allantoin, which are used to soothe the skin and improve skin texture. Going forward, the company plans to expand the technology's applications to various cosmetic formulations, including serums, creams and mists.
